title: Rachels Program V2
author: Yokozuna
desc: For Rachel to do a pull-up and get jacked.

ex.note: This is your main exercise for the day. Give it all you have. Pull all the way to the top and let yourself down slowly. Aim for 10-12 reps and either add a rep or add 5 pounds each week in phase 1.
Focus on using your chest muscles, not your shoulders. Set your shoulders back against the seat and keep your chest out all throughout the movement. 10-12 reps and progress in either reps or weight.
This will build your lats bigger which should contribute to your pull-up progress. Use a wide grip with lower weight to build your lats nice and strong. You will use a diff grip on day 3.
This is a new exercise for you and is replacing lateral raises. Sit upright and push the dumbbells above your head. Bring them down to around your ears and press back up. Check video for form.
New exercise. At the bottom you should feel a stretch in your bicep. Keeping your arms by your side, curl the weight until you feel a squeeze. Return to stretch slowly and under control. (ur cute)
Nice butt ;). These are really going to build strength in your glutes and hips so use heavier weight. Squeeze at the top and release slowly. Let's go cutie pie!
On day 3 do your pull-ups with a neutral grip. This is different than day 1 and will train your back in a different way. You may be stronger with this grip so consider upping the weight.
This is your only tricep work in this program so really make it worth it. Push yourself to failure and try to beat your previous week every time. You can cheat (use bad form) towards the end.
Second bicep of the week. If we want to see some bump on your arms then you gotta really push on these. Make sure you are feeling it in your bicep.
You should be comfortable with these by now so keep progressing week after week. If the smith is busy you can do extra lunges or leg press again instead.
Do what Alina says and focus on your glutes ;)
This will have an impact on your pull-up strength and make you look more like Lora Croft!

Look at your weight from last week and decrease it by about %15-%20. Do this weight and aim for 8 reps. For the next 4 weeks you will either add reps or  lowering weight never exceeding 10 reps.
Last weeks weight, plus 15-20%. Aim for 8 reps. Never exceed 10. If you get 10 reps, raise the weight next week to get 8. Once your hit 10, repeat. Same for each exercise. This is how we progress.
We will keep the reps range the same on this one because it will continue to provide stimulus to the lats/back without fatiguing you too much.
Take your previous weight and add 15-20%. Aim for 8-10 reps or 4 less reps than previous (whichever makes sense). Each week either add a rep or when you hit 10 reps, up the weight.
Same rep range as Phase 1. Continue to add reps or weight. We want to ramp these up so your arms start to get massive and juicy (like ur butt)
This is where we get strong! Increase the weight by 15-20% of your last week and aim for 6-10 reps or 2-4 less than the previous week. More weight + less reps = strength! Keep good squeeze and form.
Make sure your knees feel warmed up before this exercise. If you feel pain then stop. But if you feel good, getting strong on leg press will really blow up your legs. Same 15-20% rule as other lifts.
Up the weight and lower the reps by a few. Get strong in the 6-10 rep range.
Remember this is the only tricep exercise so push hard! <3 ur so hawt

This will test how close you are to doing a regular pull-up. Use 12-20% less weight than week 8 and aim for 5-8 reps. Each week increase in either reps or lowering weight never doing more than 8 reps.
Continue to make progress from phase 2. Adding more weight or reps each week. Keep target reps the same.
Maintain the same target reps as phase 2. These are an accessory to your pull-ups so we aren't going to drastically increase the weight. Again, up the reps or weight by at least a bit each week.
Take your week 8 weight and add 10-15%. Aim for 5-8 reps. This is a good strength builder for your upper body.
increase the weight by 12-20% and aim for 6-10 reps using good form. Increase a rep each week or up the weight if you exceed 10 reps.
Continue to increase your reps or weight week by week. You should continue to land between 6-10 reps. If you exceed 10, add more weight. Push these hard. Take enough rest!
Continue making progress in reps or weight. Make sure your knees feel good and warm. Slow on the way down, power on the way up but still in control of the weight.
Increase the weight and aim to land in the 6-10 rep range. Increasing quality reps each week. If you hit 11, up the weight etc.
Always beet your previous and increase the weight when you feel like you can still hit over 10 reps at that weight.
